implementation_policy: A stationary toy car is launched by a precompressed guided steel coil spring and rolls into a free wooden block. MuJoCo 3.3.7 rigid bodies: the toy car (modelled in appearance/car_model.py; tools/make_car_geometry.py writes its body surface and the shared at-rest pose into assets/scenes/spring_car_collision/toy_car) collides through the convex hull of its body and rolls on four separate wheel cylinders with bearing damping and rolling resistance; the spring is a reduced axial model (k = G d^4 / (8 D^3 n) from the wire geometry and Young's modulus, preload 60 mm, damping and guide friction) driving a 12 g pusher plate; block and added block are free boxes on the table plane z = 0. Each case starts from the same frozen at-rest initial state, the holding latch is removed at t = 0 and the case is integrated at its declared time step and sampled at 24 Hz for 4 s (physics/physics_model.py; baseline and edit DSL in scene_spec.json and edit_vocab.py). The accepted solves (assets/scenes/spring_car_collision/native_cases) are replayed in Blender 4.3.2 Cycles: appearance/render_native.py keys the 96 native samples (car, wheels, block, pusher, coil shape) and checks every frame against the cache, appearance/assets_scene.py and appearance/car_model.py build the moving parts at their physical dimensions (the car body is checked against the frozen solver geometry), appearance/look.py the room, table, lighting, materials and camera. Video frame f is native sample f-1; 1280x720, 24 fps, 96 frames. tools/export_ground_truth.py writes the per-frame ground truth from the solves; tools/publish_suite.py assembles the published suite. Material values are nominal, not calibrated.
